About me

A teacher's patience, a Customer Success Manager's focus on results

My path runs from customer service to classroom teaching to Customer Success. Each step taught me something that now shapes how I work with customers.

Customer service taught me to listen fast and solve the problem in front of me. Teaching, as a licensed educator, taught me to break complex ideas into steps people can follow. Customer Success lets me bring both together: owning the full customer lifecycle, so customers reach value sooner, adopt the product deeply, renew, and expand.

I have owned the full lifecycle for 300 B2B accounts at Blue Fish Nigeria, won back 60 of 138 lapsed key contacts, and I have guided onboarding for manufacturers on a B2B e-commerce platform at Pepagora.

My path

How I onboard

Every onboarding starts with a conversation

I do not hand every customer the same checklist. I use the same four steps with each learner, trainer and vendor.

01

Ask

A discovery conversation about what the customer wants to achieve and what matters most to them.

02

Assess

I find out how comfortable they are with digital tools, so I know how much guidance they need.

03

Plan

Onboarding milestones come directly from their answers, not from a generic template.

04

Match

I choose the format, pace and channel that fit: a Zoom walkthrough, a Loom video, a Google Meet deep dive, a lifecycle email series, or WhatsApp.

The result: customers reach value faster, adopt deeper, and have a clear reason to renew. At Digital Witch Academy this approach supported a 9 out of 10 NPS across 150+ learners and trainers.

Case study from my work

How I won back 60 of 138 lapsed key contacts

Blue Fish Nigeria, champion win back campaign ahead of the December peak.

138lapsed key contacts
60champions interviewed
43%win back rate
500 to 3,000packs from one recovered retailer

The challenge

Usage dropped across about 60 accounts, and 138 key contacts had stopped ordering as the December peak approached. Reminders and discounts would not fix a service problem, so I started with the customers.

The result

Recovered 60 of 138 lapsed key contacts. One retailer who had cut orders from 2,000 to 500 packs after two partial deliveries came back and ordered 3,000 packs for the festive season.

01

Listen first

Interviewed 60 champions to learn why they stopped ordering.

02

Find the root causes

Late delivery, short fills and damaged goods with no follow up, stockouts (24 were told stock was unavailable), and cheaper open market prices (12 champions).

03

Segment and fix

Ranked champions by value, time inactive, order history and issue, then fixed the cause with operations before offering any discount.

04

Rebuild trust

Gave realistic delivery dates and kept them, reached out first when anything slipped, and called after every delivery.

05

Monitor recovery

A health score weighted most heavily on decline in spending, with 7 and 10 day automated checks and ticket alerts. Day 30 validate, day 60 review reliability, day 90 evaluate and refine.

06

Expand

Recommended adding 60cl to the usual 50cl and 75cl, and planned festive stock with each customer.
